Command: Keep the law of a borrower
Summary: A borrower who borrows an animal or article and it is hurt or dies while the owner is absent must make it good; if the owner was present, or it was hired, the terms differ.
Commandment: Keep the law of a borrower.
Application: Borrowing is not a gift: the borrower enjoys the use, so he bears the risk of loss while it is in his hands. The rule still teaches that borrowed things are held in trust and must be made good if lost.
Purpose: To make wrongs right: the borrower who had the use of a thing answers for its loss or hurt.
